title: Theorem
body_md:
Sort implicitly the $M$ increasing chains
$\{\Delta_m(r):r\ge0\}$.  For each $q\le K_{\max}$, selecting the $q$ smallest increments yields a fixed-load optimum.  These optima are nested; the prefix minimizing the complete score~\eqref{eq:objective} is the joint MAP estimate.
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md: Consider only the first $q$ increments of each chain, since no later increment can enter a size-$q$ allocation.  By~\eqref{eq:convex}, if $\Delta_m(r)$ is selected among the $q$ smallest, every predecessor $\Delta_m(s)$, $s<r$, is smaller and is also selected.  Thus, the $q$ smallest increments automatically form a feasible union of coordinate prefixes.  Any other feasible size-$q$ selection replaces at least one of them by an increment no smaller, so its separable cost cannot be lower.  Adding the next globally smallest available increment constructs the size-$(q+1)$ optimum without changing the first $q$ selections.  Finally, for each prefix add the fixed-cardinality term $-\log\pi_q-\log(q!)$ and choose the lowest score. \hfill$\square$
head: manual

title: Proposition
body_md: If at least two loads have positive prior probability, $M\ge2$, $a>0$, and $\bm p$ is nondegenerate, then $T$ is not sufficient for $K$.
head: manual

title: Proof
body_md: Decompose the Gaussian noise into $W=\bm1^\mathsf{T}\bm Z$ and $\bm P\bm Z$.  Their cross-covariance is zero, so they are independent.  Moreover, $T=aK+W$, while $\bm R=a\bm P\bm N+\bm P\bm Z$; hence $T\perp\bm R\mid K$.  If $T$ were sufficient, it would also imply $K\perp\bm R\mid T$.  Combining the two conditional independences would make the law of $\bm R\mid K$ independent of $K$, contradicting~\eqref{eq:rmean}--\eqref{eq:rcov}.  For uniform $\bm p$, the mean vanishes but the covariance is $(\sigma^2+a^2K/M)\bm P$ on the orthogonal subspace. \hfill$\square$
head: manual
